newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDEN BOND YIELDS FALL ON UNCHANGED BUBA REPO.
newsitem.headline: SWEDEN BOND YIELDS FALL ON UNCHANGED BUBA REPO.

text.p: Swedish bond yields fell on Tuesday morning in line with other European markets in the wake of the Bundesbank's decision not to raise rates.
But the market has not completely ruled out the possibility of an imminent German hike.

"Nothing has changed. The threat that the Bundesbank will send a tightening signal to the market is still there," said Joe Prendergast, head of global foreign exchange reasearch at Credit First Boston.
The yield curve flattened to 125 from 127 basis points. Dealers said long bonds were in demand around Europe.
The six month T-bill rate was unchanged at 4.31 percent and the 10-year bond yield fell three points to 6.54 percent.
The dollar gained in strength following the Buba-decision but came off highs. The crown softened to 4.2970 crowns to the mark versus 4.2910 crowns on Monday.
"I think the strong trend for the dollar may have come to an end since speculations of a German rate hike set in," one dealer said.
U.S. inflation data is the next major focus, dealers said.
